subtitulo: Airport to hotel to the fast train, without being touted, overcharged or left behind
introPt: Quiz time. One traveller, two days, three railways and a man in an arrivals hall with a big smile. She lands at Barajas, gets herself into town, and the next morning takes the AVE south — and every single sentence she uses is one you produced out loud in this episode. Listen as many times as you like; the answers are underneath. And keep half an ear on the numbers: two of them carry that Spanish 'th', and getting them wrong is how people end up on a platform for two and a half hours.
cenario: Arrivals hall at Madrid Barajas: a tout, then the taxi rank, the fixed fare and the receipt. The next morning: the airport supplement at the ticket window, the access gate at Atocha, the track number and the luggage frame.

dialogo.pt: — Taxi? Taxi, my friend? Very cheap. (a man in the arrivals hall)
— No, thank you. (and she keeps walking, to the rank)
— Hello there. Where are we going? (the driver at the rank)

dialogo.es: ¿Me lleva a esta dirección, por favor?
dialogo.pinyin: meh YEH-bah ah EHS-tah dee-rek-THYON, por fah-BOR
dialogo.pt: — Can you take me to this address, please? (phone held up)
— It's the fixed fare, isn't it? (door still open)

dialogo.es: Sí, 33 euros dentro de la M-30.
dialogo.pinyin: see, TRAYN-tah ee tres EH-oo-rohs DEN-troh deh lah EH-meh TRAYN-tah
dialogo.tts: Sí, treinta y tres euros dentro de la eme treinta.

dialogo.es: Pare aquí, por favor. ¿Me da un recibo?
dialogo.pinyin: PAH-reh ah-KEE, por fah-BOR. meh dah oon rreh-THEE-boh
dialogo.pt: — Stop here, please. Could I have a receipt?

dialogo.pinyin: EHS-teh bee-YEH-teh BAH-leh PAH-rah el ah-eh-roh-PWEHR-toh
dialogo.pt: — (next morning, at the window) Is this ticket valid for the airport?

dialogo.es: No, el aeropuerto lleva suplemento. Son 3 euros más.
dialogo.pinyin: noh, el ah-eh-roh-PWEHR-toh YEH-bah soo-pleh-MEN-toh. son tres EH-oo-rohs mahs
dialogo.pt: — No, the airport carries a supplement. That's 3 euros extra.
dialogo.tts: No, el aeropuerto lleva suplemento. Son tres euros más.

dialogo.es: Ya tengo el billete del AVE. ¿Dónde está el control de acceso?
dialogo.pinyin: yah TEN-goh el bee-YEH-teh del AH-beh. DOHN-deh ehs-TAH el kon-TROL deh ak-THEH-soh
dialogo.pt: — I've already got my AVE ticket. Where's the access gate?

dialogo.es: Al fondo. Sale a las 11:00, vía 12. Pase ya, que cierran antes.
dialogo.pinyin: al FON-doh. SAH-leh ah lahs OHN-theh, BEE-ah DOH-theh. PAH-seh yah, keh THYEH-rrahn AHN-tehs
dialogo.pt: — Right at the end. It leaves at 11:00, track 12. Go through now — they close it early.
dialogo.tts: Al fondo. Sale a las once, vía doce. Pase ya, que cierran antes.

dialogo.pt: — Can I take this suitcase on board?

dialogo.es: Si pasa por el arco, sí. Buen viaje.
dialogo.pinyin: see PAH-sah por el AR-koh, see. bwen BYAH-kheh
dialogo.pt: — If it goes through the frame, yes. Have a good trip.

perguntas.pergunta: A man in the arrivals hall offers her a cheap taxi and she walks straight past him. Why?
perguntas.es: A man in the arrivals hall offers her a cheap taxi and she walks straight past him. Why?
opcoes: Because a real Spanish taxi is never touted — if he approached you, he isn't one
Because taxis are illegal at Spanish airports
Because he was cheaper but the journey takes longer
Because she had already booked the bus
perguntas.explica: There are three legitimate ways out: the rank ('la parada de taxis'), a ride-hailing car booked in the app and collected at the pick-up point, or the train. Anyone who comes to find you in the hall is none of those. 'No, gracias', and don't break stride.

perguntas.pergunta: What does she settle BEFORE the car moves?
perguntas.es: What does she settle BEFORE the car moves?
opcoes: Whether he takes cards
That it's the fixed airport fare
Which route he'll take
How long the journey takes
perguntas.explica: '¿Es tarifa fija, verdad?' — Madrid runs a flat €33 between Barajas and any address inside the M-30 ring, 24 hours a day, with no extras on top. Confirm it with the door still open; once you're on the ring road you have no leverage at all. If there's no fixed fare, the meter goes on — and if he refuses the meter, you get out.

perguntas.pergunta: She asks '¿Este billete vale para el aeropuerto?'. What does the clerk tell her?
perguntas.es: She asks '¿Este billete vale para el aeropuerto?'. What does the clerk tell her?
opcoes: Yes, it covers everything
Only if she validates it first
No — the airport carries a supplement, €3 extra
No — the airport is Cercanías only
perguntas.explica: The airport is almost never included. Madrid charges a €3 supplement on top of a single or ten-trip ticket; in Barcelona the airport metro (L9 Sud) is its own fare zone at about €5.90 each way and the T-casual doesn't cover it. Assume a supplement and you'll never be caught out.

perguntas.pergunta: At Atocha she opens with 'Ya tengo el billete'. What is that sentence buying her?
perguntas.es: At Atocha she opens with 'Ya tengo el billete'. What is that sentence buying her?
opcoes: It gets her out of the ticket queue and straight to the access gate
A refund on the ticket she already has
A seat upgrade
A luggage tag for the hold
perguntas.explica: 'Ya tengo el billete. ¿Dónde está el control de acceso?' does two jobs in one breath: it takes her out of a counter queue that can be forty people deep, and it points her at the only place she actually needs to be. Say it to anyone in a uniform.

perguntas.pergunta: 'Sale a las once, vía doce.' When does the train go, and from where?
perguntas.es: 'Sale a las once, vía doce.' When does the train go, and from where?
opcoes: At 11:00, from track 12
Right away ('at once'), from track 2
At 1:00, from track 12
At 11:00, from platform 2 of the metro
perguntas.explica: 'Once' is ELEVEN. It is never 'at once' — one single time is 'una vez'. It's the false friend that costs people trains, restaurant tables and tour buses. And listen to the two numbers: 'OHN-theh' and 'DOH-theh' — both carry the Spanish 'th' of 'think'. That same sound is how you tell 'cincuenta' (50) from 'sesenta' (60) when someone reads you a bill. Also: Renfe says 'vía' (track); the metro says 'andén'.

perguntas.pergunta: Why does the guard tell her to go through 'ya' — right now — when the train isn't for a while?
perguntas.es: Why does the guard tell her to go through 'ya' — right now — when the train isn't for a while?
opcoes: Because the access gate closes before the train leaves, and there's a scanner queue behind it
Because the train may leave early
Because the ticket office shuts at 11:00
Because luggage has to be checked in and loaded
perguntas.explica: A Spanish high-speed station is a small airport: X-ray, metal detector, and a gate that closes ahead of departure — the stated aim is five minutes before. Renfe's own advice is to be there 30 minutes early, and there is no late boarding. Turn up 'on time' the British way and you'll watch it leave with a valid ticket in your hand.

perguntas.pergunta: 'Si pasa por el arco, sí.' What decides whether her suitcase can come along?
perguntas.es: 'Si pasa por el arco, sí.' What decides whether her suitcase can come along?
opcoes: Whether it physically fits through the metal gauge at the gate
Its weight alone, weighed on a scale
Whether she paid a luggage fee when booking
Nothing — Spanish trains take any luggage
perguntas.explica: Renfe allows up to 3 items totalling 25 kg and 290 cm of summed dimensions, with the largest piece capped at 85 × 55 × 35 cm — and it's enforced with a physical frame at the access point. E-scooters and unicycles are banned outright. The good news: no fee, no check-in desk, no tags and nobody to argue with. It fits or it doesn't. And it's 'maleta' in Spain, never 'valija'.
